headline.definition: Full potential of today's AI and advanced-analytics applications if adopted across the economy, not a forecast, not value captured today, and not a target.
headline.method: Bottom-up, use-case-driven 'micro to macro' sizing: select use cases per sector, adjust benchmark impact to the Rwandan context, size at organisation level against a baseline, scale to sector and economy.

redistributionNote: A further ~USD 295m of company-level benefit was estimated to come at the expense of other firms, it shifts market share without adding to national output, and is excluded from the 589m figure.

sectors.driver: Increasing yields by reducing crop waste
Tax analytics, procurement savings, targeted social spending
Mining, real estate, utilities, admin and support, accommodation and food

domainSplit.note: The study also splits the 589m across 15 analytics domains (procurement analytics, fraud & debt, personalisation, throughput/yield and others). The column-to-domain pairing could not be recovered reliably from the source deck, so it is not published here. Digitising it requires the original full-potential sizing tool.

lighthouse.name: Crop-loss early warning for farmers
lighthouse.mechanism: Localised weather prediction delivered to farmers by SMS/voice, built on automatic weather stations and the national farmer registry.
lighthouse.context: Agriculture provides a livelihood to over 76% of the population and accounts for about 33% of GDP. FAO estimates farmers could be losing up to 40% of current production for want of early warning, among other risks. Mobile connectivity of 73.9% makes SMS delivery viable.
lighthouse.social: Improved national food security; greater income stability for farmers.

lighthouse.name: Bus routing and scheduling optimisation, Kigali
lighthouse.mechanism: Optimise routes and timetables to cut fuel cost and passenger waiting time.
lighthouse.benchmark: 2–5% savings in operating costs (fuel and labour)
lighthouse.context: Direct operator value only; commuter time savings are additional and were not monetised.
lighthouse.social: Time saved for citizens, lower emissions, higher on-time reliability.

lighthouse.name: Social security claims risk profiling
lighthouse.mechanism: Risk-score claims to reduce incorrect payments, wrong decision, wrong amount, or inconsistent with plan.
lighthouse.context: Applied to ~USD 98m of social benefit payouts (2019 RSSB annual report), of which roughly 70% were medical, CBHI and maternity payouts excluding pensions.
lighthouse.social: Reinforced integrity of the social security system; funds freed for legitimate claims.

lighthouse.name: Public spend and procurement analytics
lighthouse.mechanism: Spend visualisation and contract-text analytics across agencies to surface savings opportunities and contractual clauses of interest.
lighthouse.context: Government spending for FY 2021/22 was estimated at about USD 3.6bn.
lighthouse.social: Better functioning agencies; less repetitive work for staff.

lighthouse.name: Tax audit targeting and compliance scoring
lighthouse.mechanism: Advanced analytics over tax submissions to select audit cases and target inspections.
lighthouse.context: Higher taxable income recovered and fewer underreporting cases.
lighthouse.social: Helps taxpayers comply; increases budget available for national investment.

socialDimensions.name: Economic & education opportunity
socialDimensions.desc: Reduce unemployment and raise education levels through adaptive learning and targeted upskilling against future job demand.

socialDimensions.name: Socio-environment
socialDimensions.desc: Improve citizen safety and government efficiency through preventive, targeted intervention, for example better placement of schools and social services.

socialDimensions.name: Public health
socialDimensions.desc: Better health outcomes through higher-quality care and improved employee safety.

socialDimensions.name: Work life & recreation
socialDimensions.desc: Automate repetitive and tedious tasks, raising job quality, satisfaction and safety.

socialGradeNote: Each sized use case was graded 1 (low) to 3 (high) on five qualitative dimensions and averaged to a sector grade. Only use cases with a sized financial value were graded, high-social-value cases without a financial estimate are absent.

enablerInitiatives.name: National AI Innovation Lab
enablerInitiatives.desc: Matchmaker between innovators and problem statements, through targeted competitions on priority use cases that benefit many organisations.

enablerInitiatives.name: Venture builder programme
enablerInitiatives.desc: Support companies to frame AI problem statements, design architecture and find AI engineers.

enablerInitiatives.name: AI awareness and training programmes
enablerInitiatives.desc: Broad AI literacy for communities and institutions, modelled on programmes such as Finland's Elements of AI.

enablerInitiatives.name: AI Summit
enablerInitiatives.desc: Convene research, innovation, talent, financiers and ecosystem partners.

enablerInitiatives.name: Rwanda AI community
enablerInitiatives.desc: Forums, working sessions and networking to connect innovators across the country.

enablerNote: Indicative first-year operating costs from international benchmarks, as published in the 2022 study. Not budget allocations and not commitments.

context.note: Global estimate cited as the motivating context for the study.
Indicative, where data is available; the share attributable to AI is unknown.
Launching point for many government services.
Context for the agriculture use case.
Base for procurement and tax use cases.

caveats: A full-potential exercise, not a view of what can be captured in any given period.
An order-of-magnitude sizing to support directional prioritisation, not a business case for any specific investment.
Measures the potential of the technology available in 2022; it makes no assumption about later technologies, including generative AI.
Excludes the cost of capture and the investment required to realise the value.
Redeployment of freed resources is assumed but does not happen automatically; it requires reskilling and may lag.
